name: Saint Polycarp
history: Bishop of Smyrna, in what is now Turkey, and a disciple of the apostle John. He received a letter from Saint Ignatius of Antioch, who was on his way to martyrdom, and long afterwards was martyred himself, burned at the stake in old age. The account of his death, written by his own church, is the oldest record of a Christian martyrdom outside the New Testament.
life: Saint Irenaeus, who knew Polycarp as a boy, remembered him speaking of his conversations with John and others who had seen the Lord. As bishop he guarded the faith against those who twisted it, and his letter to the Philippians, full of the words of the apostles, survives. In old age he travelled to Rome to discuss the date of Easter with Pope Anicetus; they did not agree, but they parted in peace, and Anicetus invited him to celebrate the Eucharist. When persecution broke out in Smyrna, Polycarp was found at a farm outside the city. He ordered food for those who came to arrest him and asked for time to pray. In the stadium the proconsul urged him to curse Christ. He replied that he had served Christ for eighty-six years and Christ had done him no wrong: how could he blaspheme his King who had saved him? The account says the flames formed an arch around him, and he was killed with a dagger.
prayerTo: Saint Polycarp, you heard the apostles and kept their teaching whole to the end. Pray for bishops, for the elderly who keep the faith alive, and for the unity of Christians. Pray for me, that I may stay faithful to Christ all my days and, when my hour comes, offer my life to Him in thanksgiving. Amen.
penance: Polycarp fed the men who came to arrest him. Do a kindness today for someone who has treated you badly, and pray for elderly people who live alone.
meditation: Eighty-six years I have served Him, and He has done me no wrong. Look back over your own life today and count the ways Christ has been faithful to you.
